The partner's wishes govern all three
The order overrides all three
questions.explanation: Patient trust is the unifying principle across privacy, consent, and documentation duties.

questions.stem: Review: Which organization sets and enforces professional practice standards for diagnostic medical sonographers registered in Ontario?
options: Sonography Canada
OAMRS
The sonographer's employer
The CMRITO
questions.explanation: The CMRITO sets and enforces standards for its registrants; an employer's local rules do not make it the provincial regulator.

questions.stem: Review: Before an echocardiogram, the supervising sonographer notices the wrong patient's record selected on the machine, and the mismatch is corrected before scanning starts. What makes this a near miss?
options: The patient did not experience any discernible harm
The mistake was discovered by a team member
The mistake was intercepted before it reached the patient
The mistake was noticed before the report was completed
questions.explanation: Interception before reaching the patient is the defining detail of a near miss.

questions.stem: Review: Which statement best describes the different purposes of a clinical record and an organizational incident report?
options: An incident report replaces clinical documentation whenever a safety incident occurs
The clinical record supports patient care; the incident report supports safety reporting and review
A clinical record replaces an incident report if it contains all the facts
Both serve the same purpose, so the professional chooses which to complete
questions.explanation: Each serves a distinct purpose, and both processes must be followed as required.

questions.stem: Review: During a supervised echocardiogram, a capable adult patient says, "Please stop. This is uncomfortable," with several images remaining. As the student performing the scan, what is the most appropriate response?
options: Reduce the probe pressure and continue obtaining the remaining images
Explain why the remaining images are needed before stopping
Stop scanning, acknowledge the request, and involve the supervising sonographer
Pause briefly, then resume once the patient appears calmer
questions.explanation: Required images do not give permission to continue after the patient asks to stop.

questions.stem: Review: You notice that a measurement on a saved image differs from the value entered on the worksheet, and you are unsure which is correct. What should you do next?
options: Promptly describe the discrepancy to your supervisor and ask to review it together
Change the worksheet to match the saved image before mentioning the discrepancy
Wait until you can determine which value is correct before raising the concern
Leave both values unchanged and assume the interpreting cardiologist will resolve it
questions.explanation: A specific concern can be raised while you are still uncertain.

questions.stem: Which wording best raises a measurement discrepancy?
options: "You entered the wrong number."
"The value on this saved image is different from the worksheet. Can we review it together?"
"Someone messed up this study."
Nothing — assume it will resolve itself
questions.explanation: The wording identifies the evidence, makes a clear request, and does not accuse.

questions.stem: Which learning goal is demonstrated when you determine that a curious coworker's access to a record is NOT authorized?
options: Deciding whether access to patient information is authorized
Choosing the fastest examination protocol
Increasing departmental throughput
Avoiding all documentation
questions.explanation: Distinguishing technical access from authorized access is a core learning goal of this module.

questions.stem: Which action demonstrates the learning goal "describe an examination accurately in the clinical record"?
options: Recording only normal findings
Recording opinions about the patient
Recording what was completed, limitations and their reasons, and communication that actually occurred
Recording nothing when the study is limited
questions.explanation: Accurate description covers completion, limitations with reasons, and actual communication.

questions.stem: Which action demonstrates the learning goal "connect a practice question to the relevant law or standard"?
options: Choosing the shortest title
Assuming all questions concern PHIPA
Identifying whether the question concerns information, consent, documentation, protection, or regulation, and matching it to PHIPA, HCCA, CYFSA, RHPA, or CMRITO standards
Ignoring the legal dimension
questions.explanation: Matching subject matter to the correct framework is the taught method for connecting practice to law.

questions.stem: Which combination BEST reflects the closing message of this module?
options: Move quickly, avoid questions, document briefly, and remain silent
Protect information, listen to the patient, write honestly, and ask for help
Share freely, pressure gently, record rarely, and stay quiet
Diagnose independently, prescribe treatment, and discharge patients
questions.explanation: The four closing habits summarize the module's privacy, consent, documentation, and escalation duties.

questions.stem: A student is unsure whether a legal duty to report applies and considers waiting for guidance before acting. What is the correct understanding?
options: If there is a legal duty to report, seeking advice must not delay the required reporting
Reporting always waits for legal advice
Reporting is optional when uncertain
Only supervisors report
questions.explanation: Guidance may be sought, but a required report must not be delayed while waiting for advice.

questions.stem: A patient reports a new symptom during the history. Which response integrates consent, safety and communication?
options: Ignore the symptom because it is not on the order
Assess the patient's stability, pause if appropriate, involve the supervisor or responsible clinician, and document the symptom, response, and communication
Continue and mention it only if asked
Tell the patient it is irrelevant
questions.explanation: Integrated professional practice combines assessment, pausing, escalation, and documentation.

questions.stem: Which statement about being a student in this setting is correct?
options: Identify as a fully qualified practitioner for efficiency
Introduce yourself as a student, work with your supervisor, and never claim credentials or abilities you do not have
Hide your student status from patients
Perform procedures beyond training when asked
questions.explanation: Honest identification and supervised practice protect patients and support learning.

questions.stem: A patient hesitates after stopping and asks, "Will you be angry if I don't finish?" Which response is most appropriate?
options: "I'm not angry, we can stop, and I'll help you understand the options."
"We really need to finish."
"The department will be upset with me."
"It's up to your family."
questions.explanation: The response is honest, removes pressure, and supports the patient's understanding of options.

questions.stem:
Which set of statements is TRUE?

- (1) Privacy concerns the patient's rights in how information is handled. (2) Confidentiality is our duty to protect information and share only with authority. (3) Consent to the examination and consent to share information are different questions.
options: Only (1)
Only (2)
None of them
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly summarize the module's key distinctions.

questions.stem: Which combination of actions BEST represents legal responsibility in the echo lab as presented in this module?
options: Rely on logins, obtain a signature once, continue despite refusal, document only normal findings, and avoid reporting
Assume family has access, skip explanation for routine studies, complete every study regardless of refusal, and conceal errors

Check whether access to information is authorized, explain the examination and maintain consent, stop when the patient asks, record what actually happened, report when a duty applies, and ask for help when uncertain
Prioritize schedule pressure over consent, document opinions rather than facts, and escalate only when asked
questions.explanation: Each element reflects a core duty taught in this module — authorized access, maintained consent, respect for refusal, honest records, required reporting, and seeking help.
